# Cassini and Catalan identities

- [Español](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identidades_de_Cassini_y_Catalan)
- [Français](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identit%C3%A9s_de_Cassini,_de_Catalan_et_de_Vajda)
- [தமிழ்](https://ta.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%AE%95%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%9A%E0%AE%BF%E0%AE%A9%E0%AE%BF,_%E0%AE%95%E0%AF%87%E0%AE%9F%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%9F%E0%AE%B2%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D_%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%81%E0%AE%B1%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%B1%E0%AF%8A%E0%AE%B0%E0%AF%81%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%88%E0%AE%95%E0%AE%B3%E0%AF%8D)
 [Edit links](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityPage/Q4459371#sitelinks-wikipedia)                          From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia (Redirected from [Cassini's identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini%27s_identity&redirect=no))   Mathematical identities for the Fibonacci numbers

**Cassini's identity** (sometimes called **Simson's identity**), **Catalan's identity** and **Vajda's identity** are [mathematical identities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_(mathematics)) for the [Fibonacci numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_number). Cassini's identity, a special case of the other two, states that for the *n*th Fibonacci number,

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   = ( − 1  )  n   .   {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}=(-1)^{n}.}

Note here      F  0     {\displaystyle F_{0}}   is taken to be 0, and      F  1     {\displaystyle F_{1}}   is taken to be 1.

Catalan's identity generalizes this to allow     r ≠ 1   {\displaystyle r\neq 1}  :

      F  n   2   −  F  n − r    F  n + r   = ( − 1  )  n − r    F  r   2   .   {\displaystyle F_{n}^{2}-F_{n-r}F_{n+r}=(-1)^{n-r}F_{r}^{2}.}

Vajda's identity further generalizes this to allow     m ≠ n   {\displaystyle m\neq n}  :

      F  m    F  n   −  F  m − r    F  n + r   =   (  − 1  )   m − r    F  r    F  r + n − m   ,   {\displaystyle F_{m}F_{n}-F_{m-r}F_{n+r}=\left({-1}\right)^{m-r}F_{r}F_{r+n-m},}

also written as:

      F  n + i    F  n + j   −  F  n    F  n + i + j   = ( − 1  )  n    F  i    F  j   .   {\displaystyle F_{n+i}F_{n+j}-F_{n}F_{n+i+j}=(-1)^{n}F_{i}F_{j}.}

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=1)]

Cassini's formula was discovered in 1680 by [Giovanni Domenico Cassini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Domenico_Cassini), then director of the [Paris Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Observatory), and independently proven by [Robert Simson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Simson) (1753).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-Koshy-1) However [Johannes Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Kepler) presumably knew the identity already in 1608.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-2)

Catalan's identity is named after [Eugène Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eug%C3%A8ne_Charles_Catalan) (1814–1894). It can be found in one of his private research notes, entitled "Sur la série de Lamé" and dated October 1879. However, the identity did not appear in print until December 1886 as part of his collected works ([Catalan 1886](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#CITEREFCatalan1886)). This explains why some give 1879 and others 1886 as the date for Catalan's identity ([Tuenter 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#CITEREFTuenter2022), p. 314).

The Hungarian-British mathematician [Steven Vajda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Vajda) (1901–95) published a book on Fibonacci numbers (*Fibonacci and Lucas Numbers, and the Golden Section: Theory and Applications*, 1989) which contains the identity carrying his name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-West-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-4) However, the identity had been published earlier in 1960 by Dustan Everman as problem 1396 in [The American Mathematical Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_American_Mathematical_Monthly),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-Koshy-1) and in 1901 by Alberto Tagiuri in [Periodico di Matematica](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodico%20di%20Matematica).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-Tagiuri-5)

## Proof of Cassini identity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=2)]

### Proof by matrix theory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=3)]

A quick proof of Cassini's identity may be given ([Knuth 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#CITEREFKnuth1997), p. 81) by recognising the [left side of the equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sides_of_an_equation) as a [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) of a 2×2 [matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_(mathematics)) of Fibonacci numbers. The result is almost immediate when the matrix is seen to be the *n*th power of a matrix with determinant −1:

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   = det  [      F  n + 1      F  n        F  n      F  n − 1       ]  = det   [     1   1     1   0     ]   n   =   (  det  [     1   1     1   0     ]   )   n   = ( − 1  )  n   .   {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}=\det \left[{\begin{matrix}F_{n+1}&F_{n}\\F_{n}&F_{n-1}\end{matrix}}\right]=\det \left[{\begin{matrix}1&1\\1&0\end{matrix}}\right]^{n}=\left(\det \left[{\begin{matrix}1&1\\1&0\end{matrix}}\right]\right)^{n}=(-1)^{n}.}

### Proof by induction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=4)]

Consider the induction statement:

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}=(-1)^{n}}

The base case     n = 1   {\displaystyle n=1}   is true.

Assume the statement is true for     n   {\displaystyle n}  . Then:

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   +  F  n    F  n + 1   −  F  n    F  n + 1   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}+F_{n}F_{n+1}-F_{n}F_{n+1}=(-1)^{n}}        F  n − 1    F  n + 1   +  F  n    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   −  F  n    F  n + 1   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}+F_{n}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}-F_{n}F_{n+1}=(-1)^{n}}        F  n + 1   (  F  n − 1   +  F  n   ) −  F  n   (  F  n   +  F  n + 1   ) = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n+1}(F_{n-1}+F_{n})-F_{n}(F_{n}+F_{n+1})=(-1)^{n}}        F  n + 1   2   −  F  n    F  n + 2   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n+1}^{2}-F_{n}F_{n+2}=(-1)^{n}}        F  n    F  n + 2   −  F  n + 1   2   = ( − 1  )  n + 1     {\displaystyle F_{n}F_{n+2}-F_{n+1}^{2}=(-1)^{n+1}}

so the statement is true for all integers     n > 0   {\displaystyle n>0}  .

## Proof of Catalan identity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=5)]

We use [Binet's formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_number#Closed-form_expression), that      F  n   =     ϕ  n   −  ψ  n     5      {\displaystyle F_{n}={\frac {\phi ^{n}-\psi ^{n}}{\sqrt {5}}}}  , where     ϕ =    1 +   5    2     {\displaystyle \phi ={\frac {1+{\sqrt {5}}}{2}}}   and     ψ =    1 −   5    2     {\displaystyle \psi ={\frac {1-{\sqrt {5}}}{2}}}  .

Hence,     ϕ + ψ = 1   {\displaystyle \phi +\psi =1}   and     ϕ ψ = − 1   {\displaystyle \phi \psi =-1}  .

So,

     5 (  F  n   2   −  F  n − r    F  n + r   )   {\displaystyle 5(F_{n}^{2}-F_{n-r}F_{n+r})}       = (  ϕ  n   −  ψ  n    )  2   − (  ϕ  n − r   −  ψ  n − r   ) (  ϕ  n + r   −  ψ  n + r   )   {\displaystyle =(\phi ^{n}-\psi ^{n})^{2}-(\phi ^{n-r}-\psi ^{n-r})(\phi ^{n+r}-\psi ^{n+r})}       = (  ϕ  2 n   − 2  ϕ  n    ψ  n   +  ψ  2 n   ) − (  ϕ  2 n   −  ϕ  n    ψ  n   (  ϕ  − r    ψ  r   +  ϕ  r    ψ  − r   ) +  ψ  2 n   )   {\displaystyle =(\phi ^{2n}-2\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}+\psi ^{2n})-(\phi ^{2n}-\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}(\phi ^{-r}\psi ^{r}+\phi ^{r}\psi ^{-r})+\psi ^{2n})}       = − 2  ϕ  n    ψ  n   +  ϕ  n    ψ  n   (  ϕ  − r    ψ  r   +  ϕ  r    ψ  − r   )   {\displaystyle =-2\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}+\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}(\phi ^{-r}\psi ^{r}+\phi ^{r}\psi ^{-r})}

Using     ϕ ψ = − 1   {\displaystyle \phi \psi =-1}  ,

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n   (  ϕ  − r    ψ  r   +  ϕ  r    ψ  − r   )   {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n}(\phi ^{-r}\psi ^{r}+\phi ^{r}\psi ^{-r})}

and again as     ϕ =    − 1  ψ     {\displaystyle \phi ={\frac {-1}{\psi }}}  ,

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   (  ψ  2 r   +  ϕ  2 r   )   {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}(\psi ^{2r}+\phi ^{2r})}

The [Lucas number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_number#Relationship_to_Fibonacci_numbers)      L  n     {\displaystyle L_{n}}   is defined as      L  n   =  ϕ  n   +  ψ  n     {\displaystyle L_{n}=\phi ^{n}+\psi ^{n}}  , so

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r    L  2 r     {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}L_{2r}}

Because      L  2 n   = 5  F  n   2   + 2 ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle L_{2n}=5F_{n}^{2}+2(-1)^{n}}

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   ( 5  F  r   2   + 2 ( − 1  )  r   )   {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}(5F_{r}^{2}+2(-1)^{r})}       = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   2 ( − 1  )  r   + ( − 1  )  n − r   5  F  r   2     {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}2(-1)^{r}+(-1)^{n-r}5F_{r}^{2}}       = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   5  F  r   2     {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}5F_{r}^{2}}       = ( − 1  )  n − r   5  F  r   2     {\displaystyle =(-1)^{n-r}5F_{r}^{2}}

Cancelling the     5   {\displaystyle 5}  's gives the result.

Cassini and Catalan identities

# Cassini and Catalan identities

- [Español](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identidades_de_Cassini_y_Catalan)
- [Français](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identit%C3%A9s_de_Cassini,_de_Catalan_et_de_Vajda)
- [தமிழ்](https://ta.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%AE%95%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%9A%E0%AE%BF%E0%AE%A9%E0%AE%BF,_%E0%AE%95%E0%AF%87%E0%AE%9F%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%9F%E0%AE%B2%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%A9%E0%AF%8D_%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%81%E0%AE%B1%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%B1%E0%AF%8A%E0%AE%B0%E0%AF%81%E0%AE%AE%E0%AF%88%E0%AE%95%E0%AE%B3%E0%AF%8D)
 [Edit links](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityPage/Q4459371#sitelinks-wikipedia)                          From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia (Redirected from [Cassini's identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini%27s_identity&redirect=no))   Mathematical identities for the Fibonacci numbers

**Cassini's identity** (sometimes called **Simson's identity**), **Catalan's identity** and **Vajda's identity** are [mathematical identities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_(mathematics)) for the [Fibonacci numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_number). Cassini's identity, a special case of the other two, states that for the *n*th Fibonacci number,

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   = ( − 1  )  n   .   {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}=(-1)^{n}.}

Note here      F  0     {\displaystyle F_{0}}   is taken to be 0, and      F  1     {\displaystyle F_{1}}   is taken to be 1.

Catalan's identity generalizes this to allow     r ≠ 1   {\displaystyle r\neq 1}  :

      F  n   2   −  F  n − r    F  n + r   = ( − 1  )  n − r    F  r   2   .   {\displaystyle F_{n}^{2}-F_{n-r}F_{n+r}=(-1)^{n-r}F_{r}^{2}.}

Vajda's identity further generalizes this to allow     m ≠ n   {\displaystyle m\neq n}  :

      F  m    F  n   −  F  m − r    F  n + r   =   (  − 1  )   m − r    F  r    F  r + n − m   ,   {\displaystyle F_{m}F_{n}-F_{m-r}F_{n+r}=\left({-1}\right)^{m-r}F_{r}F_{r+n-m},}

also written as:

      F  n + i    F  n + j   −  F  n    F  n + i + j   = ( − 1  )  n    F  i    F  j   .   {\displaystyle F_{n+i}F_{n+j}-F_{n}F_{n+i+j}=(-1)^{n}F_{i}F_{j}.}

History

# History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=1)]

Cassini's formula was discovered in 1680 by [Giovanni Domenico Cassini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Domenico_Cassini), then director of the [Paris Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Observatory), and independently proven by [Robert Simson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Simson) (1753).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-Koshy-1) However [Johannes Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Kepler) presumably knew the identity already in 1608.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-2)

Catalan's identity is named after [Eugène Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eug%C3%A8ne_Charles_Catalan) (1814–1894). It can be found in one of his private research notes, entitled "Sur la série de Lamé" and dated October 1879. However, the identity did not appear in print until December 1886 as part of his collected works ([Catalan 1886](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#CITEREFCatalan1886)). This explains why some give 1879 and others 1886 as the date for Catalan's identity ([Tuenter 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#CITEREFTuenter2022), p. 314).

The Hungarian-British mathematician [Steven Vajda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Vajda) (1901–95) published a book on Fibonacci numbers (*Fibonacci and Lucas Numbers, and the Golden Section: Theory and Applications*, 1989) which contains the identity carrying his name.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-West-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-4) However, the identity had been published earlier in 1960 by Dustan Everman as problem 1396 in [The American Mathematical Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_American_Mathematical_Monthly),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-Koshy-1) and in 1901 by Alberto Tagiuri in [Periodico di Matematica](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodico%20di%20Matematica).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#cite_note-Tagiuri-5)

Proof of Cassini identity

# Proof of Cassini identity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=2)]

Proof by matrix theory

# Proof by matrix theory

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=3)]

A quick proof of Cassini's identity may be given ([Knuth 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassini_and_Catalan_identities#CITEREFKnuth1997), p. 81) by recognising the [left side of the equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sides_of_an_equation) as a [determinant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Determinant) of a 2×2 [matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_(mathematics)) of Fibonacci numbers. The result is almost immediate when the matrix is seen to be the *n*th power of a matrix with determinant −1:

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   = det  [      F  n + 1      F  n        F  n      F  n − 1       ]  = det   [     1   1     1   0     ]   n   =   (  det  [     1   1     1   0     ]   )   n   = ( − 1  )  n   .   {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}=\det \left[{\begin{matrix}F_{n+1}&F_{n}\\F_{n}&F_{n-1}\end{matrix}}\right]=\det \left[{\begin{matrix}1&1\\1&0\end{matrix}}\right]^{n}=\left(\det \left[{\begin{matrix}1&1\\1&0\end{matrix}}\right]\right)^{n}=(-1)^{n}.}

Proof by induction

# Proof by induction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=4)]

Consider the induction statement:

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}=(-1)^{n}}

The base case     n = 1   {\displaystyle n=1}   is true.

Assume the statement is true for     n   {\displaystyle n}  . Then:

      F  n − 1    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   +  F  n    F  n + 1   −  F  n    F  n + 1   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}+F_{n}F_{n+1}-F_{n}F_{n+1}=(-1)^{n}}        F  n − 1    F  n + 1   +  F  n    F  n + 1   −  F  n   2   −  F  n    F  n + 1   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n-1}F_{n+1}+F_{n}F_{n+1}-F_{n}^{2}-F_{n}F_{n+1}=(-1)^{n}}        F  n + 1   (  F  n − 1   +  F  n   ) −  F  n   (  F  n   +  F  n + 1   ) = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n+1}(F_{n-1}+F_{n})-F_{n}(F_{n}+F_{n+1})=(-1)^{n}}        F  n + 1   2   −  F  n    F  n + 2   = ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle F_{n+1}^{2}-F_{n}F_{n+2}=(-1)^{n}}        F  n    F  n + 2   −  F  n + 1   2   = ( − 1  )  n + 1     {\displaystyle F_{n}F_{n+2}-F_{n+1}^{2}=(-1)^{n+1}}

so the statement is true for all integers     n > 0   {\displaystyle n>0}  .

Proof of Catalan identity

# Proof of Catalan identity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cassini_and_Catalan_identities&action=edit&section=5)]

We use [Binet's formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_number#Closed-form_expression), that      F  n   =     ϕ  n   −  ψ  n     5      {\displaystyle F_{n}={\frac {\phi ^{n}-\psi ^{n}}{\sqrt {5}}}}  , where     ϕ =    1 +   5    2     {\displaystyle \phi ={\frac {1+{\sqrt {5}}}{2}}}   and     ψ =    1 −   5    2     {\displaystyle \psi ={\frac {1-{\sqrt {5}}}{2}}}  .

Hence,     ϕ + ψ = 1   {\displaystyle \phi +\psi =1}   and     ϕ ψ = − 1   {\displaystyle \phi \psi =-1}  .

So,

     5 (  F  n   2   −  F  n − r    F  n + r   )   {\displaystyle 5(F_{n}^{2}-F_{n-r}F_{n+r})}       = (  ϕ  n   −  ψ  n    )  2   − (  ϕ  n − r   −  ψ  n − r   ) (  ϕ  n + r   −  ψ  n + r   )   {\displaystyle =(\phi ^{n}-\psi ^{n})^{2}-(\phi ^{n-r}-\psi ^{n-r})(\phi ^{n+r}-\psi ^{n+r})}       = (  ϕ  2 n   − 2  ϕ  n    ψ  n   +  ψ  2 n   ) − (  ϕ  2 n   −  ϕ  n    ψ  n   (  ϕ  − r    ψ  r   +  ϕ  r    ψ  − r   ) +  ψ  2 n   )   {\displaystyle =(\phi ^{2n}-2\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}+\psi ^{2n})-(\phi ^{2n}-\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}(\phi ^{-r}\psi ^{r}+\phi ^{r}\psi ^{-r})+\psi ^{2n})}       = − 2  ϕ  n    ψ  n   +  ϕ  n    ψ  n   (  ϕ  − r    ψ  r   +  ϕ  r    ψ  − r   )   {\displaystyle =-2\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}+\phi ^{n}\psi ^{n}(\phi ^{-r}\psi ^{r}+\phi ^{r}\psi ^{-r})}

Using     ϕ ψ = − 1   {\displaystyle \phi \psi =-1}  ,

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n   (  ϕ  − r    ψ  r   +  ϕ  r    ψ  − r   )   {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n}(\phi ^{-r}\psi ^{r}+\phi ^{r}\psi ^{-r})}

and again as     ϕ =    − 1  ψ     {\displaystyle \phi ={\frac {-1}{\psi }}}  ,

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   (  ψ  2 r   +  ϕ  2 r   )   {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}(\psi ^{2r}+\phi ^{2r})}

The [Lucas number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_number#Relationship_to_Fibonacci_numbers)      L  n     {\displaystyle L_{n}}   is defined as      L  n   =  ϕ  n   +  ψ  n     {\displaystyle L_{n}=\phi ^{n}+\psi ^{n}}  , so

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r    L  2 r     {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}L_{2r}}

Because      L  2 n   = 5  F  n   2   + 2 ( − 1  )  n     {\displaystyle L_{2n}=5F_{n}^{2}+2(-1)^{n}}

     = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   ( 5  F  r   2   + 2 ( − 1  )  r   )   {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}(5F_{r}^{2}+2(-1)^{r})}       = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   2 ( − 1  )  r   + ( − 1  )  n − r   5  F  r   2     {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}2(-1)^{r}+(-1)^{n-r}5F_{r}^{2}}       = − ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n   2 + ( − 1  )  n − r   5  F  r   2     {\displaystyle =-(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n}2+(-1)^{n-r}5F_{r}^{2}}       = ( − 1  )  n − r   5  F  r   2     {\displaystyle =(-1)^{n-r}5F_{r}^{2}}

Cancelling the     5   {\displaystyle 5}  's gives the result.
